name: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA
indication: Consolidation for good risk acute myeloid leukaemia following induction chemotherapy. Relapsed disease post transplant.

drugs.special_instructions: 3000 mg/m² given TWICE daily (BD) every 12 hours on treatment days (D1, D3, D5). Administered via CADD Solis VIP pump for intermittent infusion (10:00 and 22:00). Each daily dose consists of two 3000mg/m² infusions prepared as 6000mg/m² in a single 500ml sodium chloride 0.9% bag. Each individual 3000mg/m² dose: 250ml sodium chloride 0.9% over 240 minutes at 63ml/hour. Total of 6 doses per cycle (total dose 18000mg/m²). Cytarabine dose banded according to national dose bands (100mg/ml). Connect infusion bag on day 1 and disconnect on day 2; connect on day 3 and disconnect on day 4; connect on day 5 and disconnect on day 6. CADD administration set must be used for connection to the CADD pump device. Note: regimen table (p.2) states 9am and 9pm; Regimen Summary (p.5) states 10:00 and 22:00 — confirm with dispensing pharmacist.

Continuous infusion at 0.5ml/hour via folfusor pump, administered via Y-site concurrently with cytarabine CADD pump on days 1 to 6. Disconnect folfusor at the same time as disconnecting CADD pump/cassette.

pre_medications.special_instructions: Antiemetic: ondansetron 8mg oral or intravenous 15-30 minutes prior to chemotherapy on Day 1 only. Subsequent doses are supplied as take-home medicines (twice daily days 2-7).
Antiemetic: metoclopramide 10mg oral or intravenous on Day 1 prior to chemotherapy. Subsequently supplied as take-home (three times a day when required).

take_home_medicines.frequency: Once daily (evening) on Day 1, then twice daily on days 2-7
take_home_medicines.special_instructions: Take once in the evening on Day 1 (after chemotherapy), then 8mg twice daily for 6 days (days 2-7).

take_home_medicines.frequency: Up to twice daily on Day 1, then three times daily when required
take_home_medicines.special_instructions: Take in the afternoon and evening on Day 1. Subsequently, take three times a day when required.
Antiviral prophylaxis. Take three times a day for 28 days. Supply 28 days or an original pack if appropriate.
Instil 1 drop into both eyes four times a day. Continue for 10 days (5 days after last cytarabine administration on Day 5). Conjunctivitis prophylaxis for high-dose cytarabine.
Tumour lysis prophylaxis. For first 7 days only. Not generally required where cytarabine is prescribed in the consolidation setting. Review for cycle 2 or if consolidation treatment.
Pharmacy to supply 1 x original pack.
Consider use. Pharmacy to supply 50 x 10mL pods.
Consider for patients at high risk of GI ulceration or bleed. Choice of gastric protection is dependent on local formulary choice. (Example PPI)
Consider for patients at high risk of GI ulceration or bleed. Choice of gastric protection is dependent on local formulary choice. (Example H2 antagonist)
Supportive antimicrobial. To be commenced only if and when directed by the haematology team when neutrophils are below 0.5 x10⁹/L. Supply for 28 days.
Supportive antifungal. To be commenced only if and when directed by the haematology team when neutrophils are below 0.5 x10⁹/L. Discuss choice of antifungal with consultant. Supply for 28 days.

dose_modifications.description: Patients aged 60 years and older: dose may be decreased to 1500mg/m² where the 3000mg/m² dose may not be tolerated. Also applies to patients with relapsed post-transplant disease. Discuss with consultant.
dose_modifications.action_text: Consider reducing Cytarabine to 1500mg/m² (patient aged ≥60 years or relapsed post-transplant)

dose_modifications.description: Delay treatment until neutrophils ≥ 1.0 x10⁹/L. Always check with the relevant consultant.
Delay treatment until platelets ≥ 100 x10⁹/L. Always check with the relevant consultant.
Consider blood transfusion if the patient is symptomatic of anaemia or has a haemoglobin of less than 8g/dL (80g/L).
Bilirubin > 34 µmol/L: reduce Cytarabine dose to 50% of the original dose. Escalate doses in subsequent cycles in the absence of toxicity.
Creatinine clearance < 60 ml/min: reduce Cytarabine dose to 60% of the original dose.
Creatinine clearance < 45 ml/min: reduce Cytarabine dose to 50% of the original dose.
Creatinine clearance < 30 ml/min: Discuss with consultant.

monitoring: U&Es, LFTs and FBC prior to starting a cycle of treatment
Assess cerebellar function (ataxia, nystagmus, dysarthria) before each dose — hold cytarabine and discuss with consultant if cerebellar toxicity suspected
Monitor renal function (creatinine/CrCl) prior to each cycle — dose reductions required for CrCl < 60 ml/min
Monitor hepatic function (bilirubin, AST/ALT) prior to each cycle — dose reduction required for bilirubin > 34 µmol/L
Monitor haemoglobin — consider transfusion if < 8 g/dL (80 g/L) or symptomatic anaemia
warnings: This regimen is for AMBULATORY CARE pathway use only.

CEREBELLAR TOXICITY: High-dose cytarabine (≥1000mg/m²) can cause irreversible cerebellar toxicity (ataxia, nystagmus, dysarthria). Assess cerebellar function before each dose. If cerebellar toxicity occurs, stop cytarabine immediately and discuss with consultant.

CYTARABINE SYNDROME: Fever, myalgia, bone pain, chest pain, maculopapular rash, conjunctivitis, and malaise 6-12 hours after administration. Corticosteroids may be beneficial. Prednisolone eye drops given prophylactically for conjunctivitis.
WARNING: Cytarabine is TWICE a day. TWO doses delivered in one infusion bag administered via CADD pump. Confirm pump setup before connecting.

The standard Cytarabine dose is 3000mg/m². This may be decreased to 1500mg/m² for patients aged 60 years and older, or those with relapsed post-transplant disease where the 3000mg/m² dose may not be tolerated.
All dose reductions due to adverse drug reactions should not be re-escalated in subsequent cycles without consultant approval.
If a third dose reduction is necessary, treatment should be stopped.
Cytarabine is classified as a neutral irritant (in large volumes) regarding extravasation risk.
Always refer to the patient schedule for supportive treatments and fluids.
The regimen consists of 1-2 cycles. A second cycle, if required, should proceed when there is neutrophil and platelet recovery and response to cycle one has been assessed.
Dose reductions or interruptions are not necessary for toxicities unlikely to be serious or life-threatening (e.g., alopecia, altered taste, nail changes).
